chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the slaughtered meat of the Dhimmi (people of the book under covenant), so he said: 'Do not eat it, whether he has named (God) or if he has not named (God).'
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of the People of the Book halal if they say Bismillah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that the meat of the Dhimmi is not to be eaten, regardless of whether they recited the name of God (Bismillah) during slaughter or not. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the mere profession of faith by the People of the Book does not automatically render their slaughtered animals halal, distinguishing it from the general permissibility granted in the Quran for chaste women and their food, while emphasizing the necessity of specific conditions for consumption.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Zayd Al Shahham who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about a slaughter by the Zimmy (people under the responsibility). So heasws said: ‘Do not eat it, whether he has Named (Bismillah) or if he has not Named (Bismillah)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Mufaddaf ibn Salih from Zayd af-Shahham who has said the following: “Once

abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the slaughtering of the taxpayers (who are non-Muslims). He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not use it for food even if he has mentioned the name of Allah or not.’”
